f.statement: Member States may tailor the required conditions and restrictions for risk minimisation to their national legal requirements and local healthcare systems. f.title: Set pack size appropriate to usual treatment duration
f.statement: The pack size of the medicinal product should be appropriate to the usual treatment duration. A small pack size can be useful if overdose or diversion is a risk to minimise, and adapting pack size to a prescribing interval may support therapeutic monitoring or medication review required by the SmPC.
f.clause: XVI.App1.4. Pack size

rows.quote: The pack size of the medicinal product should be appropriate to the usual treatment duration. A small pack size can be useful if overdose or diversion is a risk to minimise. Depending on the number of dosage units in the pack of a prescription-only medicine (see XVI.App1.5.), the exposure will be limited and the patient will need to see a healthcare professional at the interval corresponding to the pack size and dosing if a new prescription is necessary, thus increasing the opportunity for therapeutic monitoring and reducing the length of time a patient will be without medication review. Where the SmPC requires therapeutic monitoring or medication review at specified intervals, the adaptation of the pack size to the corresponding prescribing interval may support the effective implementation of this RMM.

f.title: Classify products as subject to medical prescription when the legal criteria are met
f.statement: Medicinal products shall be subject to medical prescription where they are likely to present a danger, directly or indirectly, even when used correctly, if used without medical supervision; are frequently and very widely used incorrectly and as a result likely to present a danger to human health; contain substances whose activity and/or adverse reactions require further investigation; or are normally prescribed to be administered parenterally.
f.clause: XVI.App1.5.1. Subject to medical prescription

rows.quote: Medicinal products shall be subject to medical prescription where: • The medicinal product is likely to present a danger either directly or indirectly, even when used correctly, if utilised without medical supervision; or • The medicinal product is frequently and to a very wide extent used incorrectly, and as a result is likely to present a direct or indirect danger to human health; or • The medicinal product contains (a) substance(s) or preparations thereof, the activity and/or adverse reactions of which require further investigation; or • The medicinal product is normally prescribed to be administered parenterally [DIR Art 71(1)].

f.title: Take the special medical prescription criteria into account when classifying a product
f.statement: When considering classification as subject to special medical prescription, the following shall be taken into account: the product contains, in a non-exempt quantity, a narcotic or psychotropic substance under international conventions; it is likely, if incorrectly used, to present a substantial risk of abuse, addiction or misuse for illegal purposes; or it contains a substance which by novelty or properties could be considered as belonging to that group as a precautionary measure.
f.clause: XVI.App1.5.2. Subject to special medical prescription

rows.quote: When considering classification of a medicinal product as subject to special medical prescription, the following shall be taken account: • The medicinal product contains, in a non-exempt quantity, a substance classified as a narcotic or a psychotropic substance within the meaning of the international conventions in force, such as the United Nations Conventions; or • The medicinal product is likely, if incorrectly used, to present a substantial risk of medicinal abuse, to lead to addiction or be misused for illegal purposes; or • The medicinal product contains a substance which, by reason of its novelty or properties, could be considered as belonging to the group envisaged in the second indent as a precautionary measure [DIR Art 71(2)].

f.title: Take the restricted medical prescription criteria into account when classifying a product
f.statement: When considering classification as subject to restricted medical prescription (which can control who may initiate treatment, prescribe and the setting of use), the following shall be taken into account: the product is reserved for treatments only followed in hospital; it treats conditions that must be diagnosed in hospital or institutions with adequate diagnostic facilities; or it is for outpatients but may produce very serious adverse reactions requiring a specialist prescription and special supervision throughout treatment.
f.clause: XVI.App1.5.3. Subject to restricted medical prescription

rows.quote: This legal status can be used to control who may initiate treatment, prescribe the medicinal product and the setting in which the medicinal product can be used. When considering classification of a medicinal product as subject to restricted medical prescription, the following shall be taken into account: • The medicinal product, because of its pharmaceutical characteristics or novelty or in the interests of public health, is reserved for treatments which can only be followed in a hospital environment; or • The medicinal product is used in the treatment of conditions which must be diagnosed in a hospital environment or in institutions with adequate diagnostic facilities, although administration and follow-up may be carried out elsewhere; or • The medicinal product is intended for outpatients but its use may produce very serious adverse reactions requiring a prescription drawn up as required by a specialist and special supervision throughout the treatment [DIR Art 71(3)].

f.title: Design patient cards with the required format, size, material, design, writable fields and language handling
f.statement: A patient card should have these features: format – single or folded card independent of the PL (not a tear-off part); size – between half a credit card and a credit card; material – carton of durable thickness, possibly laminated; design – striking and notably different from the PL; writable fields for the patient's name and, if applicable, the prescriber's name and contact details; and, if multiple language versions are bundled, it should be obvious how to take out a complete card in the preferred language.
f.clause: XVI.App2.4. Patient card
f.applicability: Patient cards

rows.quote:
For its purpose, a patient card should have the following features: • Format: single or folded (one-fold or Z-fold) card which is independent of the PL (i.e. not as a tear-
off part of the PL); • Size: at minimum the size of half a credit card and at maximum the size of a credit card, to fit inside a pocket/wallet/card holder (if more space is needed, folds can be used, see above); • Material: carton of durable thickness and possibly laminated, to sustain wear and tear over time; • Design: striking (e.g. clean layout, shapes and/or colours), to be visible and immediately identifiable as important, and notably different from the PL (i.e. not resembling a PL); • Writable fields: a field for the patient’s name and, if applicable, for the prescriber’s name and contact details; • Multiple language versions if applicable: can be bundled, but it should be obvious for the patient how to take out from the bundle a complete card in the preferred language.
